To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) person recognition is possible in social media setup, and that (2) person recognition in social network photos is a challenging problem, and that (3) the state of the arts is still far from being satisfactory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: • What are the challenges of person recognition in social photos, and how can they be overcome?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the state of the-art person recognition in social-media setup is still at its infancy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the state of the-art person recogniser [4] is not robust to the domain shift, and the recognition performance drops dramatically in challenging scenarios [1] where subjects appear in different contexts from the training.
PIPA has been used as a benchmark for person recognition on social media photos in several recent works [4][1][2][5].
PIPA is an important step towards understanding privacy in social media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
existing face recognition and pedestrian recognition algorithms do not perform well on social media photos, even when trained on the same data.
